stemBlocks.value: P = (3  -9 / a  7), Q = (-1  b / -4  1) and R = (c  -3 / -4  8). (a) Given that P + Q = R, find the values of a, b and c. (b) Solve the simultaneous equations 5x - 2y = 44 and 2x + 3y = 10 using a matrix method.
Think first: Matrix addition works position by position, so each corner of the matrices gives its own small equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p297-q08 from workbook page 297.

solutionSteps.instruction: Add the top-left entries and equate with R.
Add the top-right entries and equate.
Add the bottom-left entries and equate; check the bottom-right as well.

contentBlocks.value: a + (-4) = -4 gives a = 0; the bottom-right gives 7 + 1 = 8, which matches R.

solutionSteps.instruction: For (b), write AX = B and find the determinant.
Form the inverse and multiply it by B.

contentBlocks.value: Result: X = (8 / -2), so x = 8 and y = -2

strategyBlocks.value: Add P and Q entry by entry, equate each entry with the matching entry of R to get a, b and c, then write the equations as AX = B and use X = A inverse times B.

whyThisWorks.value: Matrices are equal exactly when all corresponding elements are equal, so a single matrix equation such as P + Q = R unpacks into four independent number equations, one for each position. For the simultaneous equations, AX = B can be solved by multiplying on the left by A inverse, since A inverse times A is the identity matrix, which leaves X alone; this works whenever det A is not zero.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to divide the final column by the determinant.

examTip.value: Substitute your x and y back into both equations. Here 5(8) - 2(-2) = 44 and 2(8) + 3(-2) = 10, so the answer is confirmed.
